status_summary: Executive Order 14187 (signed 2025-01-28) directed federal agencies to end federal support for medical transition of people under 19; a Maryland federal court preliminarily enjoined its grant-conditioning provision on 2025-03-04, and the Supreme Court held in United States v. Skrmetti (2025-06-18) that Tennessee's ban on such treatment for minors survives equal protection review. DOJ served more than 20 subpoenas on providers in June 2025, and at least six courts quashed them by 2026-01-21, with DOJ withdrawing one appeal in August 2026. CMS published a final rule on 2026-08-13 ending federal Medicaid and CHIP payment for these procedures for minors, effective 2026-10-13 and challenged in a suit filed by a 22-state coalition on 2026-09-02; the proposed hospital condition of participation rule (2025-12-19) is not final. The Foreword's call to end the practice generally is not met: it remains lawful under federal law and in many states.

timeline.event: President signs Executive Order 14187 (published 2025-02-03), which directs agencies to end federal support for medical transition of children under 19 and section 5 directs HHS to take actions that may include Medicare and Medicaid conditions of participation.

The District of Maryland in PFLAG v. Trump grants a preliminary injunction, finding the President likely lacks authority to condition federal grants on ending gender-affirming care for minors under section 4 of Executive Order 14187 and section 3(g) of Executive Order 14168.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court, District of Maryland

timeline.event: The Supreme Court decides United States v. Skrmetti (6 to 3), holding that Tennessee's law barring puberty blockers and hormones for minors for gender-identity purposes is subject to rational basis review and survives it.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: The District of Massachusetts quashes in full a DOJ subpoena to Boston Children's Hospital as issued for an improper purpose; DOJ had served more than 20 provider subpoenas on 2025-06-11, and by 2026-01-21 six courts had quashed or limited such subpoenas.
CMS proposes two rules: a Medicaid and CHIP funding prohibition for these procedures for minors and a hospital condition of participation barring them for children under 18.

CMS publishes the final Medicaid and CHIP rule barring federal funding of these procedures for minors (effective 2026-10-13, with up to six months of continued federal funding for hormone therapy already under way); the hospital condition of participation rule was not finalized.
A coalition of 22 states co-led by the Massachusetts Attorney General files suit in federal court challenging the CMS Medicaid and CHIP rule ahead of its 2026-10-13 effective date.

title: End medical sex reassignment of minors
uncertainties: HHS uses the term sex-rejecting procedures; the Foreword uses sex reassignment and calls it child abuse, which is a characterization the tracker does not adopt. The Medicaid rule is not yet effective as of 2026-10-09. The Massachusetts release does not name the court in which the coalition filed. Whether a court has been asked to stay the rule before 2026-10-13 was not found. The Crowell alert is internally inconsistent on one date and its account of the Oregon and California rulings of April and August 2026 was not independently verified, so they are not in the timeline. The PFLAG injunction scope was read from a truncated opinion excerpt and its later appeal history (Fourth Circuit) was not confirmed. The LGBTQ Nation report of the UPMC appeal withdrawal is from an advocacy outlet and gives no exact filing date. FDA actions and the Justice Department's FTC-related steps were not verified. The related record c14-08 covers Section 1557 and funding in more detail.
